note: 20 hook formulas for TikTok, written for this pack. A TikTok hook is three layers that land in the same one to three seconds: the spoken line, the text on screen, and the first visual. Each formula carries all three, plus what it is for, how it usually goes wrong, and a `match` regex so swipe.py can name a hook found in the wild. Walk them in `classify_order`, most specific first, case-insensitive. These are starting shapes, not evidence: nothing here was measured against TikTok performance data.
rules: Write the three layers separately. The spoken line, the on-screen line and the first frame each do a different job, and copying one into the other wastes a layer.
The first frame should already be moving or already show the result. A still face waiting to talk is a layer left empty.
On-screen text is read before the audio registers for anyone watching muted. Keep it to about six words.
Say the specific thing: the number, the object, the place. A hook any creator in your niche could say is not yours yet.
Pay off the promise early. A hook that holds the payoff hostage until the last second tends to get skipped by the second viewing.

hooks.name: Price Tag
hooks.template: This {thing} cost {amount}. Here is what that actually buys you.
hooks.example: This chair cost $1,400. Here is what that actually buys you.
hooks.first_visual: Hand slaps the price sticker onto the chair.
hooks.best_for: Product, money and value niches. A price is the fastest concrete thing a viewer can judge.
hooks.trap: A price with no reveal attached. The number opens a question the video has to answer.

hooks.name: Mid-Action Start
hooks.template: {Step number or stage}, and this is where most people {give up / get it wrong}.
hooks.example: Third coat of paint, and this is where most people give up.
hooks.first_visual: Brush already mid-stroke on the wall.
hooks.best_for: Process, craft and tutorial content. Starting in the middle skips the setup nobody waits for.
hooks.trap: Starting mid-action and then cutting back to the beginning. Stay in the middle and move forward.

hooks.name: The Wrong Way
hooks.template: If you {do the common thing} like this, {specific consequence}.
hooks.example: If you load your dishwasher like this, half your plates never get clean.
hooks.first_visual: Close-up of the wrong version, already in progress.
hooks.best_for: Everyday habits the viewer recognises in themselves. Comments argue, which keeps the video in circulation.
hooks.trap: A wrong way nobody actually does. The viewer has to see their own habit on screen.

hooks.name: Result Up Front
hooks.template: This is what {amount of effort} of {practice} looks like.
hooks.example: This is what 200 days of daily sketching looks like.
hooks.first_visual: The finished result fills the frame before anything else.
hooks.best_for: Transformation, skill and progress content. The result is the hook and the video earns it backwards.
hooks.trap: A result that is not visibly different from the start. If the change needs explaining, pick another formula.

hooks.name: The Typed Question
hooks.template: How do you {the exact phrase people search}? Like this.
hooks.example: How do you get candle wax out of a carpet? Like this.
hooks.first_visual: The problem itself: the wax stain, close.
hooks.best_for: Search. The spoken question mirrors what people type into TikTok search, so the video answers a real query.
hooks.trap: A question nobody types. Check it against search suggestions first, which is what /tt-seo is for.

hooks.name: Numbered Lessons
hooks.template: {N} {things} I {learned / wish I knew} after {specific experience}.
hooks.example: Four things I check before signing any apartment lease.
hooks.first_visual: The lease on a table, a pen already pointing at clause one.
hooks.best_for: Saveable advice. The number tells the viewer how long the commitment is.
hooks.trap: A number too big to deliver in the length. Seven points in 30 seconds is a list read too fast to remember.

hooks.name: Point of View
hooks.template: POV: {a specific situation the viewer has been in}.
hooks.example: POV: you said yes to helping a friend move, and they own a piano.
hooks.first_visual: The situation shot from the viewer's eye line.
hooks.best_for: Relatable comedy and shared experience. The viewer casts themselves in it.
hooks.trap: A POV so general it describes nobody. The detail at the end of the line is the joke.

hooks.name: Myth Check
hooks.template: Everyone says {common advice}. I tested it.
hooks.example: Everyone says you should rinse rice three times. I tested it.
hooks.first_visual: Two bowls side by side, labelled.
hooks.best_for: Contrarian content with proof. The test is what stops it from being an opinion.
hooks.trap: Debunking without a test. 'Actually that is wrong' with nothing on screen is just a claim.
hooks.match: \beveryone (?:says|thinks|tells you)\b|\b(?:is|is a) myth\b|\bthat'?s a myth\b|\bi tested (?:it|this|that)\b

hooks.name: I Tried It
hooks.template: I tried {the thing} for {a set time} so you do not have to.
hooks.example: I used only a paper planner for 30 days. Here is the honest result.
hooks.first_visual: The planner slammed onto a desk next to a calendar.
hooks.best_for: Experiments and reviews. The time box sets up a before and after.
hooks.trap: A result you would have predicted. If nothing surprised you, the video has no turn in it.

hooks.name: The Ranking
hooks.template: Ranking every {category} from worst to best.
hooks.example: Ranking every grocery store frozen pizza from worst to best.
hooks.first_visual: The full line-up on the counter.
hooks.best_for: Comments. People defend their favourite, which is engagement you did not ask for.
hooks.trap: Ranking things you have not tried. The audience can tell.
hooks.match: \branking (?:every|all|the)\b|\bfrom worst to best\b|\bfrom best to worst\b|\btier list\b

hooks.name: Hidden Setting
hooks.template: There is a {setting / button / feature} in {tool} that {specific benefit}.
hooks.example: There is a setting on your phone camera that fixes blurry night photos.
hooks.first_visual: Thumb hovering over the exact menu.
hooks.best_for: Tech and tool tips. Short, saveable, and easy to verify in the comments.
hooks.trap: A setting everyone knows about. Check the comments on similar videos first.

hooks.name: Comment Reply
hooks.template: {Read the viewer's comment out loud}. Fair question. Here is the answer.
hooks.example: Someone asked if this works on hardwood floors. Watch.
hooks.first_visual: The comment sticker on screen over the new attempt.
hooks.best_for: Follow-ups and community. TikTok has a native reply-with-video feature, and the comment gives the video a ready-made hook.
hooks.trap: Replying to a comment that only interests the commenter. Pick questions other people are clearly also asking.
hooks.match: ^\s*replying to\b|\b(?:someone|you guys|a lot of you|you all) asked\b|\bin the comments\b

hooks.name: Side by Side
hooks.template: {Cheap version} versus {expensive version}. Can you tell which is which?
hooks.example: A $4 knife versus a $200 knife. Can you tell which is which?
hooks.first_visual: Both items held up at the same time.
hooks.best_for: Comparison and buying advice. The viewer plays along before you answer.
hooks.trap: An obvious answer. If anyone can tell, there is no game.

hooks.name: Warning Sign
hooks.template: If your {thing} does {specific symptom}, {act now}.
hooks.example: If your car makes this noise when you brake, do not wait until Monday.
hooks.first_visual: The symptom itself, with the sound up.
hooks.best_for: Expert niches: health, cars, homes, pets. Stakes are built in.
hooks.trap: Fear without a fix. Give the next step inside the video, or it reads as bait.

hooks.name: Story Drop-In
hooks.template: My {person} just {did something unexpected}.
hooks.example: My landlord just texted me a photo of my own front door.
hooks.first_visual: The phone screen with the message, or your face reacting to it.
hooks.best_for: Storytime. The story starts at the strange part and fills in the background later.
hooks.trap: Starting with the background. 'So last year I moved into a new flat' is the third sentence, not the first.

hooks.name: Time Box
hooks.template: {Outcome} in {short specific time}.
hooks.example: A week of lunches prepped in 40 minutes.
hooks.first_visual: Timer starting, hands already moving.
hooks.best_for: Recipes, routines, productivity. The time is the promise and the edit proves it.
hooks.trap: A time that only works with a cut. If the timer jumps, someone will say so.

hooks.name: Insider Admission
hooks.template: I'm a {job}, and here is what we {do not tell / notice about} customers.
hooks.example: I'm a dental hygienist, and here is what I notice in the first ten seconds.
hooks.first_visual: You in the work setting, uniform or tools visible.
hooks.best_for: Authority, quickly. The job title is the credibility and the admission is the hook.
hooks.trap: Claiming a job you do not have, or sharing something that breaks a confidentiality rule. Check before posting.

hooks.name: Exact Viewer
hooks.template: If you {very specific situation}, watch this before {decision}.
hooks.example: If you are about to buy your first used car, watch this before you sign anything.
hooks.first_visual: The situation: a car lot, a contract, keys on a desk.
hooks.best_for: Narrow audiences with a decision coming up. The right viewer feels named.
hooks.trap: A situation too broad to feel named. 'If you want to save money' names everyone and nobody.

hooks.name: Countdown Stakes
hooks.template: I have {short time} to {goal with a consequence}.
hooks.example: I have three hours to fix this before the inspector arrives.
hooks.first_visual: A clock or a phone with the time showing, then the problem.
hooks.best_for: Challenge and vlog formats. The deadline creates a reason to stay to the end.
hooks.trap: A fake deadline. If nothing happens when the time runs out, the stakes were decoration.

hooks.name: Mistake Count
hooks.template: The {N} mistakes that make your {thing} look {bad outcome}.
hooks.example: The mistake that makes your homemade bread dense every time.
hooks.first_visual: Cutting into the dense loaf.
hooks.best_for: Problem-aware viewers. They already have the bad result and want the cause.
hooks.trap: Listing mistakes without showing the fixed version. Show both.
